title: Summarize the excerpt from 'dmoi3-tablet' (chunk 26.3) about mathematics: Notice how the negation and original statement compare. This is typical. Quantifiers and Negation. ¬ ∀ xP ( x ) is equiv
prompt: Summarize the excerpt from 'dmoi3-tablet' (chunk 26.3) about mathematics: Notice how the negation and original statement compare. This is typical. Quantifiers and Negation. ¬ ∀ xP ( x ) is equiv
true_answer: Notice how the negation and original statement compare. This is typical. Quantifiers and Negation. ¬ ∀ xP ( x ) is equivalent to ∃ x ¬ P ( x ) . ¬ ∃ xP ( x ) is equivalent to ∀ x ¬ P ( x ) . Essentially, we can pass the negation symbol over a quantifier, but that causes the quantifier to switch type. This should not be surprising: if not everything has a property, then something doesn’t have that property. And if there is not something with a property, then everything doesn’t have that property. Implicit Quantifiers. It is always a good idea to be precise in mathematics.
